catalyst.event: RV wholesale shipment cycle bottoming - Thor is the lowest-levered way to own the recovery. The 2026-09-22 fiscal Q4 print is the gate, not the reason.
catalyst.action: WAIT. Do not buy before the 09-22 print. Start the first third only after it, and only if management does not guide to a further step down in wholesale shipments. Build the rest over the following two quarters.

thesis: Thor trades at 0.82x its own book. Book value per share was 82.88 at the most recent quarter against a 67.77 close on 09-18, alongside 0.36x sales and 13.7x a trailing EPS of 4.96 that is itself depressed - net margin is 2.67% against a mid-cycle 5-7% for this industry, and ROE is 6.1%. The part that makes it ownable rather than merely cheap is the balance sheet: total debt to equity of 0.2185 and a current ratio of 1.707, with a 1.90% dividend covered at a 45% payout. A cyclical at a trough with almost no leverage does not need the cycle to turn quickly, it only needs to survive to the turn, and this one is being priced as if it might not. The 09-22 print is the gate on starting, not the reason to own it.
key_risk: The RV cycle can stay at the bottom far longer than a trough multiple suggests - these are discretionary, credit-financed big-ticket purchases and the 10-year at 4.94% is the wrong backdrop for financing one. Book value is also not a floor if the downturn extends: inventory and dealer floorplan receivables are the assets being marked, and they are exactly what impairs in a prolonged slump, so 0.82x book today can become 0.82x a smaller book.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this report is simultaneously closing LCII, an RV supplier, because Thor reports on 09-22 - so why buy the thing causing the risk. The two are consistent, and deliberately so. LCII is a stopless swing long sitting 0.6% off a 150-day low with a 138 target; the right action there is to stop owning the complex through Tuesday. THO is a different claim: accumulate the least-levered name in the same complex, after the print, over quarters, against a stated bear case rather than a stop. Neither says own the RV cycle through Tuesday morning. The second objection is that 0.82x book is cheap for a reason and the reason is the cycle. Agreed - that is what the 55 bear case prices, and it is why the entry is staged in thirds down to 58 rather than taken at once.
